author: haiku
label: c2-seed-haiku-01
changes: Numbered the steps 1 to 14 across send, fan-out and reconnect in the diagram. The original arrows had no numbers, so the flow was hard to follow.
Added a component list that says what each part does, since the original named components without explaining them.
Rewrote the terse notes as three sections: where state lives, what happens on each failure, and an open point.
Stated that the Offline Inbox stores references to messages, not copies of their bodies, and that bodies are read from Message Store.

Stated that the 30-day expiry removes inbox entries only. Messages remain in history but are no longer sent on reconnect. The original said only 'keep for 30 days' and did not say what the expiry covers.
Spelled out the online and offline sequence: send live, wait up to 5 seconds for an ack, then write the inbox entry and send the push.
Explained idempotency: the unique msg_id, the outbox written in the same transaction as the message, and the worker committing its offset only after all recipients are handled.
Added the failure cases for the relay, the worker, the gateway, presence loss and push, which the original did not cover.
Added an open point about the race between reconnect sync and a late inbox write. The original did not mention it.
Added a short opening that names the three phases (send, fan-out, reconnect) before the component list.
Added a Key terms section defining seq, ack, outbox, heartbeat and TTL, and at-least-once delivery, for readers who do not know the stack.
Explained the outbox rule in plain terms: a row exists only if its message was saved.
Stated that the 200-member cap means at most 199 recipients, and that the sender is excluded.
Clarified that the Event Bus commits its offset only after every recipient of an event is handled.
Split the Presence Registry entry description into the one-device assumption, the Gateway pointer, and the 30-second expiry.
Clarified the ack meanings: the sender's ack means saved, a recipient's ack means reached the device.
Reworded the failure notes for plain language, with the same behavior. Named the 30-day inbox expiry as a deletion, and the 'retry' case as returning the original msg_id and seq.
Fixed diagram labels for readability (for example, 'read the Presence Registry'), kept the numbered flow and arrows unchanged, and added a note that the ack arrives from the client in step 14.
Added a plain-language opening sentence that states the three phases of the design and what each one does.

Expanded the key terms so each one says what it means in this system. For example, seq is per conversation, and the outbox is explained as the reason a saved message is never lost before fan-out starts.
Spelled out 'acknowledgement' on first use and said what the sender's ack and the recipient's ack each confirm.
Defined 'online' as having a live presence entry, and 'offline' as having none or missing the 5-second ack.
Added a short definition of the Presence Registry's expiry, so a reader knows when a user stops counting as online.
Clarified the Event Bus offset rule: it is committed only after every recipient of the event is handled, so a crash replays the whole event.
Made the failure entries say what happens and what the client does next, in the same order as the flow. The meanings are unchanged.
Kept the ASCII diagram, step numbers, state locations and open point as written, since they already match the brief. The open point is restated to name the exact race.
No changes to the design itself.
